planting.note: Plant divisions in spring into cool, humus-rich, acidic soil that stays evenly moist, siting the fern where it gets dappled or full shade year-round.

directions: This circumboreal fern of high mountain screes and late-melting snowbanks forms an upright, finely cut clump that looks similar to common lady fern but with narrower, more tapered fronds and sori lacking the kidney-shaped indusium typical of Athyrium filix-femina. It wants cool roots, acidic humus-rich soil, and constant moisture, so it struggles in hot, humid lowland summers and is best suited to northern gardens or shaded rock gardens with reliable dampness. Avoid lime and direct sun, which scorch the delicate light-green fronds. Divide congested clumps in spring to maintain vigor and propagate true to type.
sources: Botanical Society of Britain and Ireland (BSBI)

planting.note: Set divisions or bulbil-raised plantlets in loose, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade in spring, keeping the crown slightly proud of the soil surface.

directions: Selected at the Dahlem Botanic Garden in Berlin, this soft shield fern forms an unusually upright, almost vase-shaped clump rather than the lax, arching habit typical of the species. Silvery croziers unfurl in spring into long, finely divided, twice- to thrice-pinnate fronds with a slight twist, deepening from pale green to a richer green as the season progresses. It is evergreen to semi-evergreen in milder climates and combines well with hostas, hellebores, and other textural shade perennials. Grow in loose, moisture-retentive but well-drained soil and shelter from harsh winter wind to keep fronds presentable through the cold months.
